newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian airline plans inflight gambling.
newsitem.headline: Australian airline plans inflight gambling.

text.p: Australia's national carrier Qantas said on Thursday it is hoping to win government approval to offer inflight gambling as part of a A$550 million (US$429 million) fleet refurbishment.

Qantas chief executive James Strong said A$320 million would be spent on new interactive video systems for all seats on its international services and most domestic flights, with the new systems capable of offering gambling services to passengers.
"Gaming would give the airline a revenue system it would not otherwise have and therefore would help offset some of the costs of installing the system," Strong told a news conference.

Qantas commercial manager Geoff Dixon said the airline was currently holding discussions with the six Australian state governments and the Australian federal government in the hope of being granted permission to offer inflight gambling.
Strong would not say what kinds of gambling were being discussed but added an unspecified maximum bet would be imposed. The service would also only be offered on international flights.
"I don't think anybody is specifically going to catch a flight in order to gamble," Strong said.
Strong said inflight gambling through interactive video was already offered on a small number of Swissair flights.
The Qantas refurbishment, which also includes high technology seating and improved amenities, will be made on all 99 of Qantas' jets over the next three years.
Dixon said Qantas was looking at an interactive video system built by Phoenix-based Interactive Flight Technologies and would make a decision on what system to use by next April.
